A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same definition-autoformalization study despite the changed title. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and the equations, figures, tables and relocated material can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v2 reports original LLM pass rates, error analyses and refinement experiments on miniF2F, Def_Wiki and Def_ArXiv, including detailed appendix results.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds GPT-4o results for autoformalization and categorical refinement in Lean4.

M1.justification: The categorical refinement, symbolic refinement and formal definition grounding procedures are retained. v3 describes applying categorical refinement to Lean4 with minor prompt modifications but specifies no new refinement steps. Prompt-FDG remains in Appendix D after moving from the main text.

E1.justification: Section 3.5 adds Lean4 as a second formalization target across miniF2F, Def_Wiki and Def_ArXiv, substantially extending language coverage beyond Isabelle/HOL. The underlying mathematical datasets and represented domains are retained.

E2.justification: Corresponding Isabelle experiments retain DeepSeekMath-7B, Llama3-8B, GPT-4o and the same comparison strategies. The Lean4 study evaluates existing zero-shot, detailed-refinement and categorical-refinement strategies; newly cited systems are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The added Lean4 experiment checks GPT-4o outputs using another proof assistant and reports pass rates without the Isabelle-specific error-category breakdown. Existing Isabelle metrics, greedy decoding and dataset splits remain unchanged. The precise Def_Wiki split used for Lean4 is not explicitly specified.

E4.justification: Section 3.5 adds a targeted generalizability analysis testing whether categorical refinement transfers to Lean4. Existing error diagnoses, SR/FDG comparisons and appendix case studies are retained; expanded discussion of semantic consistency does not add a quantitative semantic analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental confidence intervals, significance tests or repeated-run/seed counts. Dataset means and standard deviations are unchanged, and the new Lean4 results follow the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: v3 adds the Lean4 results in Table 4: detailed refinement and CR-SYN achieve 15.98% and 16.80% on miniF2F; detailed refinement and CR-UDF achieve 7.14% and 10.71% on Def_Wiki. All refinement variants tie at 6.67% on Def_ArXiv. Matched Isabelle results throughout the main text and appendices are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation of autoformalization and the definitions and code examples are retained. Neither version contains theoretical guarantees or proofs that change. The new common-versus-specialized distinction is conceptual framing rather than a formal mathematical development.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same benchmark, error-analysis and refinement/grounding contributions, including the headline 16% and 43% figures. Dropping the emphatic statement that grounding is 'fundamental' does not otherwise redefine the central claims.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations distinguishing common definitions with implicit preliminaries from specialized definitions with explicit context, and expands its rationale for small datasets. Appendix B discusses overlap between syntactic checks and semantic validity. Section 3.5 adds a transfer interpretation while explicitly leaving Lean4 adaptations of SR and FDG outside scope.

D1.justification: v3 newly reports a dataset quality check targeting diversity and complementary challenges. This is a limited disclosure; its operational criteria and the exact Lean4 prompt modifications are not supplied. Existing collection instructions, Isabelle prompts, greedy decoding and code/data access information are retained, often relocated.

R1.justification: v3 adds literature on Lean, autoformalization pipelines and semantic judging, including LeanDojo, Jiang et al. (2024), ATLAS and Zhang et al. (2025). Related work more explicitly distinguishes the definition datasets from exercise-oriented generated corpora, while retaining the original research positioning.

P1.justification: The paper is retitled, the dataset rationale and related-work passages are substantially rewritten, and the main-text/appendix organization changes extensively. Dataset construction moves to Appendix A, Prompt-FDG moves to Appendix D, and the error taxonomy moves into the main text. Affiliations, acknowledgements and terminology are also edited.

P2.justification: Figure 2 changes from four small panels in one row to a larger two-by-two arrangement. Multiple tables are resized or relocated, code-example boxes are removed, and the two prompt tables are consolidated onto one page. A Lean4 results table is added, while existing Isabelle data displays retain their numerical content.

improvement.justification: The Lean4 study partly addresses v2's untested transfer beyond Isabelle, and the enlarged Figure 2 improves readability. Negative Prompt-FDG results remain available in Appendix D. The gains are limited: Lean4 testing covers only GPT-4o, categorical refinement adds no benefit over detailed feedback on Def_ArXiv, implementation details remain sparse, and semantic consistency is still not quantitatively evaluated.
